title: CodeNib: A Multi-View Data System for Serving Repository Context to Coding Agents
event_hint: CodeNib reusable multi-view repository context runtime
problem: Coding agents repeatedly rediscover repository facts because lexical, dense, structural, live-language, and task-local history systems are disconnected. Edits affect each view differently, and without explicit commit/range validity boundaries, build, maintenance, query, and context-delivery costs remain hidden.
mechanism: CodeNib compiles per-commit lexical, dense, and structural views, maps results to repository-relative source ranges, and tracks artifact status/configuration in a manifest. View-specific maintainers repair graphs and reuse content-addressed vectors; the runtime loads only needed views, provides ranked search, static/live symbol navigation, and bounded context through a unified interface, and records provider/view/token traces.

evidence.claim: Across 100 repository snapshots, median graph and vector updates that matched independent rebuilds were 8.7x and 25.4x faster.
On the static-navigation subset matching normalized live-server locations, median per-request live/static latency ratio was 4.7x.
Across five models, selected context policies preserved localization while using 50–87% fewer trajectory tokens than paired grep/read.
evidence.condition: Lowest-token core arm meeting a common localization margin

evidence.claim: Graph updates matched independent rebuilds on 15/33 source-changing transitions and vector updates on 28/31 transitions.

The runtime separates quality, compatibility, update fidelity, latency, and token usage across retrieval, navigation, maintenance, and bounded context delivery rather than collapsing them into one score.

evaluation_context: CodeNib is evaluated over 100 snapshots and multiple lifecycle stages: retrieval/reranking, dense-index construction/search, static/live navigation, incremental maintenance, and bounded context delivery. Reported agent-context results cover five models and paired grep/read baselines; patch generation and concurrent production updates are explicitly outside the study.
limitations: Only updates whose outputs matched an independent rebuild received speedup claims; graph fidelity matched in 15/33 transitions and vector fidelity in 28/31, leaving unmatched transitions unresolved in the excerpt. Static navigation matches normalized locations on 632/1,000 requests, so live-server substitution is not universal. The study evaluates localization/context serving rather than patch generation, task success, or production concurrent updates, and view construction/maintenance costs may dominate small repositories (inference).
project_relevance: For Agent acceleration, CodeNib provides a data-lifecycle pattern: reusable per-commit views, explicit validity/manifest status, source-range alignment, and operation-specific bounded context policies. It suggests measuring build/update fidelity, warm query latency, live/static fallback rate, context tokens, and duplicate Read/Grep calls separately instead of claiming a single indexing speedup (inference).
